items.q: What are the five love languages, and who do they apply to?
items.a: Gary Chapman's five: **words of affirmation**, **quality time**, **acts of service**, **physical touch**, and **receiving gifts**. Vinh treats them as a **connection superpower** for romantic partners, family, friends, and colleagues — not romance only.

items.q: Why does care often get lost even when both people are trying?
items.a: We default to speaking **our own** love language. Vinh poured words; his wife showed **acts of service** — both loved, neither felt it, until they translated. Unspoken mismatch means love gets **lost in translation**.

items.q: What is the fastest way to diagnose your primary love language?
items.a: Use the **hurt-test**: which absence stings first — ignored entry, no time together, no help offered, forgotten gift occasions, or physical distance? The fastest sting reveals your primary language.

items.q: What rule replaces 'treat others how you want to be treated'?
items.a: Treat others how **they** want to be treated. Practicing a foreign language feels weird (gifts can feel shallow; touch can feel forced) — do it **for them**, not for your comfort, and do not judge their language.

items.q: How do you identify someone else's love language?
items.a: **Covert**: observe what would hurt them most when missing (approximate). **Overt**: send this video and ask directly (accurate). Write each person's language somewhere you see daily — after **10+ years**, Vinh still needs the cue.

items.q: What concrete moves speak each love language well?
items.a: Words: use the **SNI framework** (Spot, Name, Impact) regularly. Quality time: **phone away**, undivided attention. Acts of service: **1–3 daily tasks**, never bail. Touch: small consistent contact. Gifts: thoughtful tokens, not expensive splurges.

items.q: What mindset closes the gap when habits pull you back to your own language?
items.a: **Love is always a choice. Connection is always a choice.** Defaulting to your own language is one of the **hardest habits to break** — visible reminders and deliberate practice keep care landing.
